notes_summary: Mid-market product org trialed Hosted API; positive on latency/quality. Now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost. Ask: capacity sizing and traffic forecast to build committed contract.
notes:
- Background: EmberLake builds an in-app conversational assistant + semantic search for a B2B customer base (CRM integrations). Mid-market (400 employees), product led but sales motion shifting to enterprise.
- Initial Hosted API trial (2 weeks): developers integrated chat endpoints and fast proof-of-concept. Trial metrics below.
- Key asks: predictable throughput (dedicated), VPC networking, audit logs, SSO + KMS, quantization options for cost reduction, and deterministic tail latency for interactive use.
- Trial performance (observed): avg QPS 48 (non-peak), sustained baseline ~30 QPS during workday, observed peak bursts ~210 QPS (short spikes), peak concurrency ~170 concurrent open sessions during demo burst. Avg tokens per chat response: ~110 tokens; generation-heavy flows avg 220 tokens when including assistant + context. Embeddings: ~12% of calls, ~512 tokens equivalent per embedding call (note: embeddings are vector heavy but lower token cost). 18% of traffic is reranking calls (shorter responses, avg 30 tokens). ~25% of requests expect streaming responses (progressive UX) which affects concurrency.
- Cost sensitivity: product team prioritizes lower per-token unit cost for high-volume routes (search, embeddings). They're open to model fallbacks (smaller cheaper model for straightforward queries) but need consistent quality for customer-facing assistant.
- Dedicated sizing ask (from SE call): forecast profile for 12-month commit covering expected growth:
    * Current baseline: 30-50 QPS sustained (weekdays)
    * Expected steady-state (6 months): 120-180 QPS sustained as feature rolls out to more accounts
    * Peak planning: 450-600 QPS burst capacity during product launches and demo periods (short 10-20 minute windows)
    * Concurrency planning: target support for 400 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled
    * Token mix: 55% short-chat (<=120 tokens), 25% long-chat (>120 tokens), 12% embeddings, 8% reranking/analytics
    * Avg token per req (weighted): ~95 tokens; peak bursts see avg ~160 tokens
- SE notes on capacity: would recommend a hybrid pool approach: mix of lower-cost quantized instances for bulk chat and a small pool of high-performance GPUs for long-form generation and low-latency tails. Suggest initial Dedicated pool equivalent to 8-12 A100-80GB GPUs (or 6 H100 for better perf) with autoscale burst to additional 8 GPUs for peak events. Include KV-cache sizing: expected working set ~120M tokens; cache hot-hit rate target 30-40% to reduce token cost and latency.
- Reliability/rollout needs: canary traffic routing, per-model fallbacks, per-route cost & latency dashboards. Redwood Console features were demoed and EmberLake liked token-level cost breakdowns.
- Security/procurement: procurement requested SOC2 Type 2 evidence, KMS integration doc, and data residency guarantees for EU customers. Finance asked for committed price band and overage rates.
- Quotes from stakeholders: "Latency matters more than raw cost for customer-facing assistant; but embeddings volume is where we'll optimize for price." — Head of Product. "We need sizing that won't surprise us in QPS bursts; can you show cost vs reserve vs burst math?" — VP Engineering.
- POC milestones: technical deep-dive scheduled (Mar 15), security review kickoff (Mar 10), draft contract & pricing expected to procurement (Apr 1).
- Open items / blockers: finalize GPU type and burst SLA, confirm VPC peering architecture and egress policy, finalize retention period for telemetry and audit logs, estimate committed vs overage pricing scenarios.
- Next actions for AE/SE: produce dedicated-capacity sizing doc (QPS/concurrency -> GPU count & memory plan) + three pricing scenarios (conservative/expected/aggressive) and send by 2026-03-12; set up deep-dive with infra team for H100 perf comparison.
